001package io.jstach.rainbowgum;
002
003import java.io.IOException;
004import java.io.UncheckedIOException;
005import java.net.URI;
006import java.util.Comparator;
007import java.util.EnumSet;
008import java.util.List;
009import java.util.Objects;
010import java.util.Set;
011import java.util.TreeSet;
012
013import org.jspecify.annotations.Nullable;
014
015/**
016 * Renders a diagnostic report of a bound {@link RainbowGum}: which sections are included
017 * ({@link Section#VERSION}, {@link Section#COMPONENTS}, {@link Section#METRICS},
018 * {@link Section#ALERTS}) depends on how the {@link Builder} that created this reporter
019 * was configured.
020 *
021 * @apiNote The rendered output's format carries <strong>no compatibility guarantee
022 * whatsoever</strong>. It is meant to be read by a human, or an agent, while setting
023 * things up or debugging an incident, not parsed by anything expecting a stable schema,
024 * and may change between any two releases including patch releases.
025 */
026public sealed interface LogReporter permits DefaultLogReporter {
027
028        /**
029         * Writes the report for the given RainbowGum directly to the given appendable, rather
030         * than building the whole report in memory first, so a caller can stream straight
031         * into a {@link java.io.Writer}/response even while the system is in a degraded
032         * state.
033         * @param gum bound RainbowGum instance to report on.
034         * @param appendable destination.
035         * @throws IOException if the appendable throws.
036         */
037        void report(RainbowGum gum, Appendable appendable) throws IOException;
038
039        /**
040         * Writes the report to a {@link StringBuilder}, which never actually throws
041         * {@link IOException} in practice, so callers do not need to handle one.
042         * @param gum bound RainbowGum instance to report on.
043         * @param sb destination.
044         */
045        default void report(RainbowGum gum, StringBuilder sb) {
046                try {
047                        report(gum, (Appendable) sb);
048                }
049                catch (IOException e) {
050                        throw new UncheckedIOException(e);
051                }
052        }
053
054        /**
055         * Renders the report as a String.
056         * @param gum bound RainbowGum instance to report on.
057         * @return report.
058         */
059        default String report(RainbowGum gum) {
060                var sb = new StringBuilder();
061                report(gum, sb);
062                return sb.toString();
063        }
064
065        /**
066         * Implemented by a component that wants to contribute its own description to a report
067         * instead of falling back to just its class name. Entirely optional: nothing in this
068         * codebase or a custom {@link LogOutput}/{@link LogEncoder} implementation is
069         * required to implement this.
070         *
071         * @apiNote a {@link LogOutput} implementing this does <strong>not</strong> get the
072         * same "no overlapping calls" guarantee {@link LogOutput}'s other methods are
073         * promised: a report can be requested from an unrelated thread (e.g. an operator
074         * pulling diagnostics) at any time, including while the appender is concurrently mid
075         * write/flush/reopen on its own thread. {@link #report(Appendable)} must therefore be
076         * safe to call concurrently with itself and with every other {@link LogOutput}
077         * method, unlike the rest of that interface's contract.
078         */
079        interface Reportable {
080
081                /**
082                 * Returns a concise description of a component. A {@link Reportable} supplies its
083                 * own description; ordinary named classes use their canonical name, while
084                 * anonymous, synthetic, and local classes use the supplied fallback.
085                 * @param component component to describe.
086                 * @param fallback description for a component without a stable class name.
087                 * @return component description.
088                 */
089                static String toString(Object component, String fallback) {
090                        if (component instanceof Reportable reportable) {
091                                var out = new StringBuilder();
092                                try {
093                                        reportable.report(out);
094                                }
095                                catch (IOException e) {
096                                        return fallback;
097                                }
098                                return out.toString();
099                        }
100                        var type = component.getClass();
101                        if (type.isAnonymousClass() || type.isLocalClass() || type.isSynthetic()) {
102                                return fallback;
103                        }
104                        var name = type.getCanonicalName();
105                        return name != null ? name : fallback;
106                }
107
108                /**
109                 * Writes this component's own description directly to the given appendable.
110                 * @param out destination.
111                 * @throws IOException if the appendable throws.
112                 */
113                void report(Appendable out) throws IOException;
114
115        }
116
117        /**
118         * A section of the report that can be independently turned on or off.
119         */
120        enum Section {
121
122                /**
123                 * Rainbow Gum's own version, printed first if included.
124                 */
125                VERSION,
126                /**
127                 * The wired component tree: active global properties, then each router's
128                 * publisher, appenders, outputs, and encoders.
129                 */
130                COMPONENTS,
131                /**
132                 * Metrics from {@link LogConfig#metrics()}.
133                 */
134                METRICS,
135                /**
136                 * Recent entries from {@link LogConfig#alerts()}, see
137                 * {@link Builder#maxAlerts(int)}.
138                 */
139                ALERTS,
140                /**
141                 * Logger names registered via
142                 * {@link LogConfig.LoggerRegistry#registerLoggerName(LoggerAPI, String)}, each
143                 * with its resolved level, see {@link Builder#loggerLevels(boolean)}.
144                 */
145                LOGGERS,
146                /**
147                 * The distinct set of {@link LoggerAPI}s registered via
148                 * {@link LogConfig.LoggerRegistry#registerLoggerName(LoggerAPI, String)}, e.g.
149                 * seeing both {@code SLF4J} and {@code JUL} means both facades are in active use
150                 * (not just on the classpath).
151                 */
152                FACADES;
153
154        }
155
156        /**
157         * Creates a builder.
158         * @return builder.
159         */
160        static Builder builder() {
161                return new Builder();
162        }
163
164        /**
165         * Builds a {@link LogReporter}.
166         */
167        final class Builder {
168
169                private static final Set<Section> DEFAULT_SECTIONS = EnumSet.of(Section.VERSION, Section.COMPONENTS);
170
171                private static final LogFormatter DEFAULT_ALERT_FORMATTER = LogFormatter.builder()
172                        .text("[")
173                        .timeStamp()
174                        .text("] ")
175                        .level()
176                        .text(" ")
177                        .loggerName()
178                        .text(" - ")
179                        .message()
180                        .build();
181
182                private final EnumSet<Section> sections = EnumSet.noneOf(Section.class);
183
184                private int maxAlerts = 5;
185
186                private LogFormatter alertFormatter = DEFAULT_ALERT_FORMATTER;
187
188                private boolean loggerLevels = true;
189
190                private Builder() {
191                }
192
193                /**
194                 * Replaces the set of sections to print. An empty set is treated the same as
195                 * never calling this method at all: the default sections
196                 * ({@link Section#VERSION}, {@link Section#COMPONENTS}) are used.
197                 * @param sections sections to print.
198                 * @return this.
199                 */
200                public Builder sections(Set<Section> sections) {
201                        this.sections.clear();
202                        this.sections.addAll(sections);
203                        return this;
204                }
205
206                /**
207                 * Adds a single section to print, in addition to any already added.
208                 * @param section section to print.
209                 * @return this.
210                 */
211                public Builder section(Section section) {
212                        this.sections.add(section);
213                        return this;
214                }
215
216                /**
217                 * Maximum number of most recent alerts to print when {@link Section#ALERTS} is
218                 * included. Oldest-first entries beyond this count are omitted, not truncated mid
219                 * list. Default is 5.
220                 * @param maxAlerts maximum alerts to print, zero or greater.
221                 * @return this.
222                 */
223                public Builder maxAlerts(int maxAlerts) {
224                        if (maxAlerts < 0) {
225                                throw new IllegalArgumentException("maxAlerts must be zero or greater: " + maxAlerts);
226                        }
227                        this.maxAlerts = maxAlerts;
228                        return this;
229                }
230
231                /**
232                 * Formatter used to render each alert entry when {@link Section#ALERTS} is
233                 * included. Alerts are just {@link LogEvent}s (see {@link LogAlerts#dump()}), so
234                 * any {@link LogFormatter} works here, e.g. one that omits the timestamp for a
235                 * deterministic report. Default prints
236                 * <code>[timestamp] LEVEL loggerName - message</code>.
237                 * @param alertFormatter formatter for a single alert.
238                 * @return this.
239                 */
240                public Builder alertFormatter(LogFormatter alertFormatter) {
241                        this.alertFormatter = Objects.requireNonNull(alertFormatter);
242                        return this;
243                }
244
245                /**
246                 * Whether to resolve and print each logger's level, via
247                 * {@link LogConfig#levelResolver()}, next to its name when
248                 * {@link Section#LOGGERS} is included. Default is <code>true</code>.
249                 * @param loggerLevels false to print just the bare logger names.
250                 * @return this.
251                 */
252                public Builder loggerLevels(boolean loggerLevels) {
253                        this.loggerLevels = loggerLevels;
254                        return this;
255                }
256
257                /**
258                 * Builds the reporter.
259                 * @return reporter.
260                 */
261                public LogReporter build() {
262                        Set<Section> resolved = sections.isEmpty() ? DEFAULT_SECTIONS : EnumSet.copyOf(sections);
263                        return new DefaultLogReporter(resolved, maxAlerts, alertFormatter, loggerLevels);
264                }
265
266        }
267
268}
269
270record DefaultLogReporter(Set<LogReporter.Section> sections, int maxAlerts, LogFormatter alertFormatter,
271                boolean loggerLevels) implements LogReporter {
272
273        /*
274         * Every one of these is already a named constant in LogProperties, printed as
275         * "key = value" rather than modeled as a new type, since none of these is a leaf on
276         * the component tree below: they are process wide context that colors how to read
277         * everything that follows.
278         */
279        private static final List<String> GLOBAL_PROPERTY_KEYS = List.of(LogProperties.GLOBAL_CHANGE_PROPERTY,
280                        LogProperties.GLOBAL_QUEUE_LEVEL_PROPERTY, LogProperties.GLOBAL_QUEUE_ERROR_PROPERTY,
281                        LogProperties.GLOBAL_ANSI_DISABLE_PROPERTY, LogProperties.GLOBAL_APPENDER_REENTRANT_LOCK_PROPERTY,
282                        LogProperties.GLOBAL_THREADLOCAL_DISABLED_PROPERTY, LogProperties.GLOBAL_OPTIMIZE_PROPERTY);
283
284        /*
285         * Every section is separated from the next by exactly one blank line, added here
286         * rather than left to each appendXxx method to manage its own leading/trailing
287         * newline: that previously meant whether a blank line actually showed up between two
288         * sections was an accident of which of the two happened to append one (VERSION and
289         * METRICS did, COMPONENTS/ALERTS/LOGGERS did not), so e.g. COMPONENTS immediately
290         * followed by METRICS printed with no separating blank line at all.
291         */
292        @Override
293        public void report(RainbowGum gum, Appendable out) throws IOException {
294                boolean first = true;
295                if (sections.contains(LogReporter.Section.VERSION)) {
296                        first = appendSeparator(out, first);
297                        appendVersion(out);
298                }
299                var config = gum.config();
300                if (sections.contains(LogReporter.Section.COMPONENTS)) {
301                        first = appendSeparator(out, first);
302                        appendComponents(out, gum, config);
303                }
304                if (sections.contains(LogReporter.Section.METRICS)) {
305                        first = appendSeparator(out, first);
306                        appendMetrics(out, config.metrics());
307                }
308                if (sections.contains(LogReporter.Section.ALERTS)) {
309                        first = appendSeparator(out, first);
310                        appendAlerts(out, config.alerts());
311                }
312                if (sections.contains(LogReporter.Section.LOGGERS)) {
313                        first = appendSeparator(out, first);
314                        appendLoggers(out, config);
315                }
316                if (sections.contains(LogReporter.Section.FACADES)) {
317                        first = appendSeparator(out, first);
318                        appendFacades(out, config);
319                }
320        }
321
322        private static boolean appendSeparator(Appendable out, boolean first) throws IOException {
323                if (!first) {
324                        out.append("\n");
325                }
326                return false;
327        }
328
329        private void appendVersion(Appendable out) throws IOException {
330                out.append("Rainbow Gum ").append(RainbowGumVersion.VERSION).append("\n");
331        }
332
333        private void appendComponents(Appendable out, RainbowGum gum, LogConfig config) throws IOException {
334                appendGlobalProperties(out, config.properties());
335                out.append("Debug mode: ").append(config.debugMode().toString()).append("\n");
336                out.append("\n");
337                for (var router : routersOf(gum.router())) {
338                        appendRouter(out, config, router);
339                }
340        }
341
342        private void appendGlobalProperties(Appendable out, LogProperties properties) throws IOException {
343                out.append("Properties: ");
344                LogPropertiesReporting.describe(out, properties);
345                out.append("\n");
346                out.append("Global Properties:\n");
347                for (String key : GLOBAL_PROPERTY_KEYS) {
348                        String value = properties.valueOrNull(key);
349                        out.append("  ").append(key).append(" = ").append(value == null ? "(unset)" : value).append("\n");
350                }
351        }
352
353        private static List<LogRouter.Router> routersOf(LogRouter.RootRouter root) {
354                return switch (root) {
355                        case SingleRootRouter s -> List.of(s.router());
356                        case CompositeLogRouter c -> List.of(c.routers());
357                        /*
358                         * Neither of these carries a real, fully bound set of named routers: both are
359                         * pre-bind/queueing states (GlobalLogRouter.INSTANCE is the "nothing bound
360                         * yet" default, delegating to a QueueEventsRouter until a real RainbowGum
361                         * binds). report(RainbowGum, ...) is only ever called with an already-bound
362                         * instance, so these are unreachable in practice, not a real gap.
363                         */
364                        case QueueEventsRouter q -> List.of();
365                        case GlobalLogRouter g -> List.of();
366                };
367        }
368
369        private void appendRouter(Appendable out, LogConfig config, LogRouter.Router router) throws IOException {
370                String name = router instanceof SimpleRouter sr ? sr.name() : router.getClass().getSimpleName();
371                out.append("Router: ").append(name).append("\n");
372                appendPublisher(out, config, name, router.publisher());
373        }
374
375        private void appendPublisher(Appendable out, LogConfig config, String routeName, LogPublisher publisher)
376                        throws IOException {
377                out.append("  Publisher: ")
378                        .append(publisher.getClass().getSimpleName())
379                        .append(publisher.synchronous() ? " (synchronous)" : " (asynchronous)")
380                        .append("\n");
381                /*
382                 * LogRouter.Router.Builder.build() registers the Appenders it hands to the
383                 * publisher factory under this same route name (see there), so this works for any
384                 * publisher, current or future, that uses Appenders.asList()/asSingle() the
385                 * ordinary way, with no cooperation required from the publisher itself.
386                 * resolvedOrNull() is null only if the publisher never called either one, which
387                 * means it does not use the appenders this ordinary way at all.
388                 */
389                var apps = config.serviceRegistry().findOrNull(LogAppender.Appenders.class, routeName);
390                var resolved = apps == null ? null : apps.resolvedOrNull();
391                if (resolved == null) {
392                        /*
393                         * Reportable is the escape hatch for a publisher that does something unusual
394                         * and does not go through Appenders normally at all, same as
395                         * appendOutput/appendEncoder.
396                         */
397                        if (publisher instanceof Reportable r) {
398                                out.append("    ");
399                                r.report(out);
400                                out.append("\n");
401                        }
402                        else {
403                                out.append("    (no appender information available for ")
404                                        .append(publisher.getClass().getSimpleName())
405                                        .append(")\n");
406                        }
407                        return;
408                }
409                for (var appender : resolved) {
410                        for (var direct : directAppendersOf(appender)) {
411                                appendAppender(out, direct);
412                        }
413                }
414        }
415
416        private static List<DirectLogAppender> directAppendersOf(LogAppender appender) {
417                return switch (appender) {
418                        case CompositeLogAppender c -> List.of(c.appenders());
419                        case DirectLogAppender d -> List.of(d);
420                        default -> List.of();
421                };
422        }
423
424        private void appendAppender(Appendable out, DirectLogAppender appender) throws IOException {
425                out.append("    Appender: ").append(appender.name()).append("\n");
426                out.append("      Type: ").append(appender.getClass().getSimpleName()).append("\n");
427                if (appender instanceof AbstractLogAppender a) {
428                        out.append("      Flags: ").append(a.flags.toString()).append("\n");
429                }
430                appendOutput(out, appender.output());
431                appendEncoder(out, appender.encoder());
432        }
433
434        private void appendOutput(Appendable out, LogOutput output) throws IOException {
435                out.append("      Output: ")
436                        .append(output.getClass().getSimpleName())
437                        .append(" (type=")
438                        .append(output.type().toString());
439                URI uri = uriOrNull(output);
440                if (uri != null) {
441                        out.append(", uri=").append(LogRedactor.redactUri(uri));
442                }
443                if (output instanceof Reportable r) {
444                        out.append(", ");
445                        r.report(out);
446                }
447                out.append(")\n");
448        }
449
450        private static @Nullable URI uriOrNull(LogOutput output) {
451                try {
452                        return output.uri();
453                }
454                catch (UnsupportedOperationException e) {
455                        return null;
456                }
457        }
458
459        private void appendEncoder(Appendable out, LogEncoder encoder) throws IOException {
460                /*
461                 * No accessor on LogEncoder itself for describing its own configuration beyond
462                 * its concrete class: Object#toString() is not a safe fallback since most
463                 * implementations never override it. A component that wants to contribute more
464                 * can implement Reportable instead, entirely opt-in: see FormatterEncoder for the
465                 * one built-in example.
466                 */
467                out.append("      Encoder: ").append(encoder.getClass().getSimpleName());
468                if (encoder instanceof Reportable r) {
469                        out.append(" (");
470                        r.report(out);
471                        out.append(")");
472                }
473                out.append("\n");
474        }
475
476        private void appendMetrics(Appendable out, LogMetrics metrics) throws IOException {
477                out.append("Metrics:\n");
478                for (var metric : metrics.snapshot()) {
479                        out.append("  ")
480                                .append(metric.name())
481                                .append(" = ")
482                                .append(Long.toString(metric.value()))
483                                .append(" (")
484                                .append(metric.level().toString())
485                                .append(")\n");
486                }
487        }
488
489        private void appendAlerts(Appendable out, LogAlerts alerts) throws IOException {
490                var stats = alerts.stats();
491                out.append("Alerts (total=")
492                        .append(Long.toString(stats.total()))
493                        .append(", capacity=")
494                        .append(Integer.toString(stats.capacity()))
495                        .append("):\n");
496                var dump = alerts.dump();
497                int show = Math.min(dump.size(), maxAlerts);
498                StringBuilder line = new StringBuilder();
499                for (var event : dump.subList(dump.size() - show, dump.size())) {
500                        line.setLength(0);
501                        alertFormatter.format(line, event);
502                        out.append("  ").append(line).append("\n");
503                }
504        }
505
506        private void appendLoggers(Appendable out, LogConfig config) throws IOException {
507                out.append("Loggers:\n");
508                /*
509                 * DefaultLoggerRegistry is the only implementation (LogConfig.LoggerRegistry
510                 * deliberately does not expose the accumulated names itself, see its javadoc);
511                 * downcasting here is the same pattern DefaultLogConfig's own constructor uses to
512                 * reach DefaultLogAlerts#addInternalListener.
513                 */
514                var registry = (DefaultLoggerRegistry) config.loggerRegistry();
515                for (String name : new TreeSet<>(registry.loggerNames())) {
516                        out.append("  ").append(name);
517                        if (loggerLevels) {
518                                out.append(" = ").append(config.levelResolver().resolveLevel(name).toString());
519                        }
520                        out.append("\n");
521                }
522        }
523
524        private void appendFacades(Appendable out, LogConfig config) throws IOException {
525                out.append("Facades:\n");
526                var registry = (DefaultLoggerRegistry) config.loggerRegistry();
527                var apis = new TreeSet<LoggerAPI>(Comparator.comparing(Object::toString));
528                apis.addAll(registry.loggerAPIs());
529                for (var api : apis) {
530                        out.append("  ").append(api.toString()).append("\n");
531                }
532        }
533
534}
